name: RPM
about: RPM is the ad revenue you earn for every thousand pageviews. It is the publisher's headline yield metric because it captures fill, price and ad density in one number tied to your actual traffic.

name: Seller eCPM
about: Seller eCPM is the effective revenue you earn per thousand paid impressions, whatever the pricing model behind them. It lets you compare CPM, CPC and flat-fee demand on one scale.

name: Publisher ARPU
about: Publisher ARPU is the ad revenue earned per unique user over a period. It shifts the question from how much a page is worth to how much an audience member is worth, which matters for subscriptions and first-party data strategy.

name: Revenue per Available Ad Slot
about: Revenue per available ad slot measures what every ad opportunity earns, filled or not, quoted per thousand slots. Like RevPAR in hotels, it punishes unsold inventory, so it is the truest read of total yield.
formulaDisplay: Revenue per 1,000 slots = (Ad revenue ÷ Available ad slots) × 1000

name: Fill Rate
about: Fill rate is the share of ad requests that returned a paid ad. Unfilled requests are revenue left on the table, but chasing 100% fill with cheap demand can drag down eCPM.

name: Viewable Fill Rate
about: Viewable fill rate is the share of ad requests that became a paid and viewable impression. With buyers increasingly paying on viewability, it is the fill number that predicts what you can actually sell.
formulaDisplay: Viewable fill rate = (Viewable filled impressions ÷ Ad requests) × 100

name: Ad Load
about: Ad load is the average number of ads served per pageview. More ads raise revenue in the short run but slow pages, cut viewability and wear out readers, so it is the dial to set with care.
formulaDisplay: Ads per pageview = Ad impressions ÷ Pageviews

name: Header Bidding Win Rate
about: Header bidding win rate is the share of a bidder's bids that won the auction. A bidder that bids often but rarely wins is adding latency without adding revenue.

name: Header Bidding CPM Uplift
about: CPM uplift is how much higher your average CPM is with header bidding than it was with a waterfall. It is the number that justifies, or questions, the latency and complexity of adding bidders.
formulaDisplay: CPM uplift = ((CPM with HB − CPM before) ÷ CPM before) × 100

name: Publisher Take-Home Rate
about: Take-home rate is the share of each advertiser dollar that actually reaches the publisher after every intermediary fee. Supply-path studies regularly find it well below what either side assumes.
formulaDisplay: Take-home rate = (Publisher net revenue ÷ Advertiser gross spend) × 100

name: PG Realization Rate
about: PG realization rate is the share of booked programmatic guaranteed revenue that actually delivered and billed. Gaps usually come from targeting that is too narrow, creative issues or buyer-side pacing.
formulaDisplay: Realization rate = (Delivered PG revenue ÷ Booked PG revenue) × 100

name: Direct Revenue Mix
about: Direct revenue mix is the share of ad revenue that comes from deals you sold directly rather than open auctions. A healthy direct share means steadier prices and less dependence on exchange demand.
formulaDisplay: Direct revenue mix = (Direct-sold revenue ÷ Total ad revenue) × 100
